sections.h2: What should I know before selling a house in Randolph?
sections.html:
Randolph Township requires a fire inspection for the sale of a one- or two-family house, and appointments fill up fast because the Fire Prevention Bureau holds them in a single weekly morning window. Book the slot as soon as you have a closing date.

Randolph is a 21-square-mile Morris County township with a high owner-occupancy rate, so owner-occupied houses make up most of the market. Whether you list, sell privately or accept an as-is cash purchase, the inspection and the deed recorded in Morristown apply to the house.

sections.h2: How large is Randolph and what do its housing figures show?
sections.html:
The 2020 census counted 26,504 people in Randolph, and the estimate for mid-2025 is 26,878. Nearly four in five households own their home, and 91.7% of residents stayed at the same address over the prior year, which shows a stable population.

sections.h2: How did Randolph begin and which communities make up the township?
sections.html:
The Lenni Lenape were the first inhabitants, and Quakers followed. New Jersey's first iron mine opened here in 1713, and the area supplied the Continental Army during the winter encampment at nearby Jockey Hollow. Hartshorne Fitz-Randolph bought 1,000 acres around Mine Hill in 1753, and the township took his name. The legislature incorporated it on January 1, 1806, out of Mendham Township.

In the early 20th century it became a vacation area known for woods, ponds and lakes, with farms, large hotels and bungalow colonies through the 1950s. Today the township is made up of named communities that appear in addresses and listings:

  • Center Grove, Fernbrook, Ironia and Shongum, each also the name of an elementary school.
  • Mount Freedom, Mount Fern, Mill Brook and Youngstown.
  • Calais and Black River Pond.

Several towns were carved out of Randolph over the years, including Dover, Wharton, Mine Hill and Victory Gardens, so check that a plat or survey names the right municipality.

sections.h2: How do the hills and weather affect a Randolph property?
sections.html:
The township lies in the New Jersey Highlands, with flat-topped ridges and deep valleys. Land ranges from 551 to 1,120 feet above sea level, and the State Planning Commission has designated the township half rural and half suburban. The township sits upstream of the Black River, the South Branch of the Raritan, the Whippany River and the Rockaway River.

Recorded temperatures range from a high of 102 degrees in 1953 to a low of minus 24 in 1943. July is the warmest month and September has the heaviest average precipitation. If your lot is on a slope or beside a stream, collect any drainage or retaining wall records before listing. If the house uses a well or septic system, ask the township and county offices which records a buyer's lender will want.

sections.h2: How do roads and transit connect Randolph to the region?
sections.html:
Route 10, Dover-Chester Road (County Route 513) and Sussex Turnpike (County Route 617) pass through the township. Randolph maintains 119.53 of its 144.95 miles of roadway, with Morris County responsible for 19.62 miles and the state for 5.80. Workers report a mean commute of 30.3 minutes.

NJ Transit route 875 serves the township, and the local MCM2 and MCM7 bus routes were cut because of budget constraints. Buyers who commute without a car should check current schedules before they make an offer.

sections.h2: Which schools and parks serve Randolph homes?
sections.html:
Randolph Township Schools enrolled 4,220 students in 2022-23 across six schools: Center Grove, Fernbrook, Ironia and Shongum elementary schools, Randolph Middle School and Randolph High School, which had 1,349 students. County College of Morris opened in 1968 on a 222-acre campus in the township.

The township runs several large recreation sites:

  • Brundage Park, 232 acres, with lighted courts and fields, a four-mile paved trail and a playhouse.
  • Freedom Park, 172 acres, with football, lacrosse and baseball fields.
  • Randolph Park, 41 acres, with a beach and docks for lap swimming.
  • Heistein Park, 44 acres, with soccer fields and a lake for fishing and skating.
  • Stonybrook Park, 30 acres, with a summer day camp and swimming pool.

sections.h2: What does the Randolph smoke detector inspection require?
sections.html:
The township's page calls it the Certificate of Smoke Detector, Carbon Monoxide Alarm and Secondary Power Source Identification. It applies to the sale, rental or change of occupancy of a one- or two-family dwelling and comes from the New Jersey Uniform Fire Code. The fee is $100 for the first inspection and $100 for each reinspection, or $150 if the inspection is requested on another day. The Fire Official's office takes bookings on 973-989-7039, and inspections run Monday mornings from 9:30 to 11:30.

The standards differ by the age of the house:

  • Every level needs a smoke detector, including the basement, with one in the hall outside each bedroom and none more than about 10 feet from a bedroom.
  • Homes built before 1977 may use battery detectors, but changeable-battery units are no longer accepted, so choose sealed 10-year batteries.
  • Homes built in 1977 or later, or with a substantial addition, must keep their hard-wired detectors working and interconnected, and may not replace them with battery types.
  • A carbon monoxide alarm goes outside the bedrooms on each level that has them.
  • A central station alarm system must work fully, including battery backup, with sounders loud enough to reach each bedroom at 70 decibels with the door closed.

sections.h2: What is the secondary power label and what else might Randolph ask for?
sections.html:
A house with generators, solar panels or battery storage must carry a label within 18 inches of the main electrical panel and meter. It reads similar to "CAUTION: MULTIPLE SOURCES OF POWER" and cannot be handwritten. A label that meets ANSI Z535.4 satisfies the rule. Put one up before the inspector arrives.

The township fee schedule also lists a letter stating that a certificate of occupancy is not required for a change of title. Ask the Building Department whether your sale qualifies for that letter and what it costs now.

sections.h2: What state fee brackets and recording steps apply to a Randolph sale?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state realty transfer fee. For consideration above $350,000, the Division of Taxation lists $5.30 per $500 for the portion from $550,000 to $850,000, which covers the area around Randolph's $670,700 median value.

Deeds go to the Morris County Clerk's Registry department, which is open from 8:00 am to 4:00 pm. Every land document needs a cover sheet and a cover letter with the submitter's name and address. Each document must also carry "Record and Return" or "Cancel and Return" instructions, and a return envelope should be large enough for the deed. The Registry's phone is 973-285-6130.

sections.h2: Which sale route fits a Randolph owner?
sections.html:
A listing makes sense when the house is in good shape and you have a few months. Plan for a clean inspection report and a closing date that allows for the Monday morning slot.

An as-is cash sale shifts repair risk to the buyer. You still need the inspection certificate, so compare which party orders it and who pays a failed visit's reinspection. If tenants live in the house, remember that the same certificate applies to rentals and changes of occupancy.

faqs.q: Does Randolph require an inspection when I sell my house?
faqs.a: Yes. A smoke detector, carbon monoxide alarm and secondary power source certificate is needed for the sale of a one- or two-family dwelling. The Randolph Fire Prevention Bureau performs it.

faqs.q: How much does the Randolph fire inspection cost?
faqs.a: The first inspection is $100 and each reinspection is $100. An inspection requested on another day costs $150. Appointments run Monday mornings from 9:30 to 11:30 and fill up quickly.

faqs.q: Can I use battery smoke detectors in my Randolph house?
faqs.a: Only in some cases. Homes built before 1977 may use battery units, and they must have sealed 10-year batteries. Homes built in 1977 or later, or with a substantial addition, must keep hard-wired interconnected detectors working.

faqs.q: Where is a Randolph deed recorded?
faqs.a: The Morris County Clerk's Registry department records it, with a cover sheet attached to the document. Registry recording hours are 8:00 am to 4:00 pm.

faqs.q: What transfer fee applies to a Randolph sale near the median home value?
faqs.a: The seller pays the state realty transfer fee. A $670,700 sale falls between $550,000 and $850,000, where the Division of Taxation schedule lists $5.30 per $500 for that portion of the price.
